\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{لولا} (lawlā)}{لولا (lawlā)}]{\ar{لولا} (lawlā) — if not for}

\label{lesson:AR-C400-lawla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for as long as, then the Arabic for otherwise.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{لولا}}
\textbf{\ar{لولا}} — \emph{lawlā} — \textquotedblleft{}if not for\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{لولا} \ar{المطر} \ar{لذهبنا} \ar{إلى} \ar{البحر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{lawlā al-maṭar la-dhahabnā ilā al-baḥr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If not for the rain, we would have gone to the sea.
\end{quote}

The result takes \ar{لـ}, as after \ar{لو}: \ar{لولا} … \ar{لـ} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{لولا}} (\emph{lawlā}) is built from the native Arabic \emph{law}, \textquotedblleft{}if\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{lā}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}: if it were not for. The deeper origin of such particles is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lawlā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lawlā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{lawlā al-maṭar la-dhahabnā ilā al-baḥr.} — If not for the rain, we would have gone to the sea.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for as long as, then the Arabic for otherwise, then say \emph{lawlā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{لولا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}If not for\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مهما} (mahmā)}{مهما (mahmā)}]{\ar{مهما} (mahmā) — whatever}

\label{lesson:AR-C400-mahma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for otherwise, then the Arabic for if not for.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مهما}}
\textbf{\ar{مهما}} — \emph{mahmā} — \textquotedblleft{}whatever\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{مهما} \ar{حدث،} \ar{سأبقى} \ar{صديقك}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mahmā ḥadatha, sa-abqā ṣadīqak.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Whatever happens, I will stay your friend.
\end{quote}

Like other condition words, it is often followed by the past: \ar{مهما} \ar{حدث}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مهما}} (\emph{mahmā}) is a native Arabic particle of condition, whatever. Grammarians usually trace it to \emph{mā}, \textquotedblleft{}what\textquotedblright{}, said twice; its origin is not settled.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahmā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahmā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mahmā ḥadatha, sa-abqā ṣadīqak.} — Whatever happens, I will stay your friend.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for otherwise, then the Arabic for if not for, then say \emph{mahmā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{كلما} (kullamā)}{كلما (kullamā)}]{\ar{كلما} (kullamā) — whenever}

\label{lesson:AR-C400-kullama}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for if not for, then the Arabic for whatever.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{كلما}}
\textbf{\ar{كلما}} — \emph{kullamā} — \textquotedblleft{}whenever\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{كلما} \ar{زرت} \ar{جدتي،} \ar{طبخت} \ar{لي}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kullamā zurtu jaddatī, ṭabakhat lī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Whenever I visit my grandmother, she cooks for me.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{كلما}} (\emph{kullamā}) joins \emph{kull}, \textquotedblleft{}all, every\textquotedblright{}, built on the native Arabic root \emph{k-l-l} (Lane), with \emph{mā}: every time that, whenever.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kullamā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for if not for, then the Arabic for whatever, then say \emph{kullamā} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{سواء} (sawāʾ)}{سواء (sawāʾ)}]{\ar{سواء} (sawāʾ) — whether}

\label{lesson:AR-C400-sawa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for whatever, then the Arabic for whenever.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{سواء}}
\textbf{\ar{سواء}} — \emph{sawāʾ} — \textquotedblleft{}whether\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{سنخرج} \ar{سواء} \ar{أمطرت} \ar{أم} \ar{لا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sa-nakhruju sawāʾ amṭarat am lā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We will go out whether it rains or not.
\end{quote}

It pairs with \ar{أم}: \ar{سواء} … \ar{أم} ….

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{سواء}} (\emph{sawāʾ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{s-w-y}, \textquotedblleft{}to be equal, level\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Sawāʾ} is equality: it is all the same, whether one thing or the other.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sawāʾ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sa-nakhruju sawāʾ amṭarat am lā.} — We will go out whether it rains or not.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for whatever, then the Arabic for whenever, then say \emph{sawāʾ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{أينما} (aynamā)}{أينما (aynamā)}]{\ar{أينما} (aynamā) — wherever}

\label{lesson:AR-C400-aynama}



\begin{quote}

\textbf{\ar{أينما}} — \emph{aynamā} — \textquotedblleft{}wherever\textquotedblright{}.
